summary: This paper proposes Neighbor Distance Minimization (NDM), an unsupervised method for decomposing neural network representation spaces into interpretable orthogonal subspaces motivated by a mutual-exclusiveness hypothesis about feature groups. The core idea is novel and well-motivated: minimizing within-subspace nearest-neighbor distances finds rotations that concentrate dependent features together, provably reducing total correlation between subspaces. Toy model experiments convincingly demonstrate the method works in a controlled setting, and GPT-2 Small evaluations with known circuits provide meaningful quantitative support. The main gaps are the absence of variance/error bars on all quantitative results, quantitative evaluation limited to a single 117M-parameter model, and a preliminary 2B-model evaluation that is more exploratory than rigorous.
strengths: Genuine novelty: unsupervised decomposition of representation space is a new and under-explored direction in mechanistic interpretability; previous subspace methods (DAS, etc.) require human-specified causal models.

The mutual-exclusiveness / feature-group hypothesis is theoretically grounded and connects naturally to prior work on multi-dimensional superposition (Engels et al., 2024), giving the method a principled underpinning.
Toy model evaluation is clean and rigorous — access to ground-truth features allows unambiguous validation that NDM recovers correct subspaces from indirect objectives.

The GPT-2 test suite is well-constructed: five tests across two known circuits with Gini coefficient as a concentration metric, five diverse baselines (Identity, Random, PCA1/2, SAE-Feature), and multiple normalization variants (raw, dimension-normalized, variance-normalized).
The MI-based subspace merging procedure to determine dimension configuration is principled and avoids a free hyper-parameter over number of subspaces.
Honest discussion of limitations: Linear Representation Hypothesis dependency, compute constraints, coarse partition granularity, and unexplained small subspaces are all acknowledged.

key_concerns.issue: No variance or error bars on any quantitative result. Table 1 (the primary quantitative claim) reports single numbers with no confidence intervals, standard deviations across seeds, or significance tests. It is impossible to assess whether NDM's 0.71 average Gini coefficient is reliably above the 0.60 threshold or whether the gap over the Feature baseline is statistically real.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report results over at least 3 random initialization seeds for the orthogonal matrix R and include standard deviations in Table 1. A simple paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test across the five test conditions would suffice to establish statistical significance over the best baseline.

key_concerns.issue: Quantitative evaluation is entirely limited to GPT-2 Small (117M parameters). The 2B-model experiments (Qwen2.5-1.5B, Gemma-2-2B) use a knowledge-conflict patching protocol where no ground-truth circuits are available, making it impossible to quantify how well NDM recovers the true decomposition. The strong generality claim in the title and abstract is not supported by any rigorous experiment beyond GPT-2 Small.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either construct a comparable quantitative test suite for at least one of the 2B models (e.g., using recently published circuits for factual recall in Gemma), or explicitly reframe the 2B results as exploratory / qualitative in the abstract and conclusion.

key_concerns.issue: The MI merging threshold is a critical hyperparameter for the entire pipeline, but its sensitivity is relegated to App. G.4 and the main text provides no ablation. Since the dimension configuration c entirely determines what the orthogonal rotation is trained to do, threshold sensitivity directly bears on reproducibility and reliability.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Include a concise sensitivity table in the main paper (2–3 threshold values × the five GPT-2 tests) so readers can assess robustness without consulting the appendix.

key_concerns.issue: The qualitative evaluation (Sec. 5.2) is centered on InversionView ([Author] et al., 2024b), a tool the reviewers cannot independently assess because the reference is anonymized under double-blind policy. This is not a violation of double-blind rules, but the qualitative narrative of Section 5.2 is difficult to evaluate critically since the interpretability tool itself is opaque to reviewers.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Provide a self-contained description of the preimage-retrieval procedure used (Section E.1 seems to do this for the vector-search variant) and include enough of InversionView's methodology in an appendix to make the qualitative evaluation independently assessable.

key_concerns.issue: Apparent typographic error in the method description: R is written as R ∈ R^{d×d²} in Eq. (4), which is dimensionally inconsistent with the orthogonality constraint R^T R = I applied to a square rotation of R^d.

The abstract has fragmented sentence structure (several sentences are clearly run-on or merge two thoughts), and several passages in the main text exhibit similar grammatical roughness that reduces clarity.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Careful copy-editing pass, particularly on the abstract and Section 2's 'Feature Groups and Subspaces' paragraph.

questions_for_authors: How sensitive are the Gini coefficient results in Table 1 to different random seeds for initializing R? Is the reported ordering of methods consistent across seeds?

In the 2B-model experiments (Sec. 5.3), how do you rule out the possibility that the differential patching effect simply reflects subspaces of different sizes rather than mechanistically distinct routing circuits? Can you show that a size-matched baseline also fails to separate the two effects?

The merging criterion merges two subspaces when their MI exceeds a threshold; what happens to the final dimension configuration as the threshold is varied? Specifically, does NDM degrade gracefully or are there sharp phase transitions?

Algorithm 1 is referenced in the main text but appears only in the appendix. Why is the core algorithm not included in the main paper, and are there space-budget reasons or was this an intentional structural choice?

Footnote 1 references 'a web application' for extended qualitative results. Can you confirm the application will be released upon de-anonymization, and is there any way to make the qualitative evaluation available to reviewers during the rebuttal period without compromising anonymity?

Is the Euclidean distance choice in Eq. (3)–(4) theoretically motivated or purely empirical? The text says cosine similarity performs worse in preliminary experiments — can you characterize when and why this matters?
calibration_check: The paper's core claims — that NDM finds more concentrated subspace representations than baselines in GPT-2 Small, and that separate subspaces mediate context vs. parametric knowledge in 2B models — are supported by the presented evidence, but the absence of variance estimates and the exploratory nature of the 2B experiments means the generality implied in the abstract and conclusion is somewhat ahead of the rigorous evidence.

significance.justification: Unsupervised representation-space decomposition could become a standard pre-analysis step in mechanistic interpretability, enabling input-independent circuit construction; impact depends on whether the method scales and generalizes beyond GPT-2 Small.

novelty.justification: NDM is a genuinely new direction: all prior subspace methods require human-specified causal models or supervision, and the mutual-exclusiveness / feature-group hypothesis motivating the objective has not been formalized or exploited this way before.

rigor.justification: Toy model analysis is rigorous and the MI-total-correlation connection is sound; GPT-2 evaluation is reasonable; but the 2B-model evaluation lacks controls, and the MI interpretation of the loss is described as heuristic rather than proven.

statistical_soundness.justification: No variance, error bars, or significance tests appear anywhere in the quantitative results; all numbers in Table 1 are single-run point estimates, making it impossible to assess whether reported improvements over baselines are statistically reliable.

calibration_honesty.justification: Limitations are listed concretely (granularity, Linear Representation Hypothesis dependency, unexplained small subspaces, compute constraints), and the 2B results include an explicit caveat about unknown circuits; the abstract slightly overclaims generality given that rigorous evaluation is on GPT-2 Small only.

clarity.justification: The geometric intuition in Section 3 is well-explained and Figure 1b caption is descriptive, but the abstract is grammatically fragmented, Algorithm 1 is absent from the main text, and several paragraphs (especially in Sec. 2) are hard to parse due to run-on sentences.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard conference structure is followed; Related Work appearing inside a Discussion section is unconventional but acceptable; the paper fits within typical ICLR length with appropriate appendix offloading.

reproducibility.justification: The optimization objective, KSG-based MI estimator, and dimension-merging procedure are described in enough detail for reproduction; however, Algorithm 1 is in the appendix, the KSG threshold is not specified in the main text, and the qualitative evaluation depends on an anonymized tool, collectively introducing non-trivial friction.

related_work.justification: Coverage is broad and fair across components, SAEs, and subspace methods; the positioning against DAS/supervised subspace discovery is clear; the discussion of multi-dimensional superposition (Engels et al., 2024) is appropriately thorough; a direct comparison to ICA or other classical ICA-style methods as baselines would strengthen positioning.

figure_quality.justification: From captions, Figure 3 (four preimage panels for different subspaces encoding token, prior token, position, and topic) and Figure 5 (differential patching under two counterfactual types) appear well-designed and directly support the central claims; Figure 1 multipanel serves double duty for motivation and toy-model validation.

breadth_generality.justification: Rigorous quantitative evaluation covers only GPT-2 Small with five test instances drawn from two known circuits; the 2B experiments are semi-quantitative and exploratory; a second model class or additional circuit types in the main test suite would substantially strengthen generality claims.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline accept: the contribution is novel and the core evidence is sound, but the lack of variance estimates in Table 1, the narrow quantitative scope (GPT-2 Small only), and the sensitivity of the key hyperparameter being uncharacterized in the main paper are significant enough gaps to require revision before acceptance.
